title: First Commands! [whoami, pwd, expr, and cd]
description:
You may be kinda sick of just `Ctrl-C Ctrl-V` over and over. Don't worry, as it's time for you to learn your first ever commands!

---
I belive i should explain filesystems first:
When you get a file in linux, it is represented as a _filepath_. This will look somthing like this: `~/linux-start-assets/transactions`. ~: this means your root. For me, it is actually `/home/lucar/linux-start-assets/transactions`. Files are actually just a tree, so for this, it would look like this:
```
root
  └── home
    └── lucar
        └── linux-start-assets
```

For actual commands, first, somthing simple:
### Command 1:  `pwd`.
This stands for "Print Working Directory". Basically this prints where you are. In Linux, ~ means /home/YOUR_USERNAME, so in my Linux, ~ = `/home/lucar`. Here is what pwd outputs for me in my ~/cli directory:
```
lucar@DESKTOP-08KNEMT:~/cliCode$ pwd
/home/lucar/cliCode
```
Pretty Simple, Right?

---
### Command 2: `cd`.
cd stands for _Change Directory_. This, as you may expect, allows you to change the directory you are in. It uses a path like normal, so you just need to run `cd ~` to go to home.
### Command 3: `whoami`:
This is what it says. It just prints your username.
### Command 4 `expr`:
Another simple one! expr just preforms math. `expr 123456 + 7890` runs 123456 + 7890, and you can use + - / *.
# Assignment:
Use `cd` to go to the `STARTER_FILE_YOU_INSTALLED_NAME/accounts` directory. Submit the lesson from **within _that directory_**.
